claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 8 (under 16)
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'd be happy to help you check your eligibility for Child Benefit! Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking you about your child or children.

**How old are the children you're enquiring about?** 

Please let me know:
- The name(s) of your child/children
- Their age(s)

This will help me understand which category they fall into, as Child Benefit eligibility depends partly on the child's age. Generally:
- **Under 16**: Likely to qualify
- **16-19**: May qualify if they're in approved education or training
- **20 or over**: Generally not eligible

Once you provide these details, I can guide you through the rest of the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I have one child - Alex, who's 8 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thanks for providing that information. Alex is 8 years old, so he falls into the **under 16** category, which means he's likely to qualify.

Let me continue with the next question in the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check the next eligibility requirement:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or not in paid work at all?**

Since Alex is 8 years old, I'm guessing he's not in employment, but I want to confirm this for the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all - he's only 8! He's still in primary school.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! That's perfectly clear - Alex isn't working, so he meets that requirement. Let me continue with the next eligibility check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question:

**Is Alex NOT receiving certain benefits in his own right?**

Specifically, we need to check if he's receiving:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA), or
- Universal Credit

Since Alex is 8 and in primary school, I expect the answer is no - he's not receiving these benefits - but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex doesn't get any benefits in his own name. He's just a child.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex doesn't receive those benefits. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Next question about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex NOT in a disqualifying apprenticeship?**

Given that Alex is 8 and in primary school, he's definitely not in any kind of apprenticeship. So this should be straightforward - but I want to confirm that he's not in any apprenticeship at all (regardless of type).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, definitely not - he's only 8! He's far too young for any apprenticeship.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is clearly not in any apprenticeship. Let me move forward to the next stage of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now we need to check residency requirements. This is an important part of eligibility for Child Benefit.

**Where do you normally live?** 

To qualify for Child Benefit, you (the claimant) generally need to:
- Normally live in the UK, OR
- Meet certain special circumstances (such as having settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or working/studying abroad with pre-settled status, etc.)

Could you tell me:
1. Do you normally live in the UK?
2. If not in the UK, do you have any special status or circumstances that might apply (for example, EU Settlement Scheme status, or working abroad as a Crown servant)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm in Manchester.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You live in the UK, which means you meet the residency requirement. Let me continue to the next part of the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your responsibility for Alex.

**Are you responsible for Alex?**

This means one of the following:
1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying for things like food, clothes, housing, pocket money, etc. - at least equivalent to what Child Benefit would provide), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement towards Alex's care

Which of these applies to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You live with Alex, so you clearly meet the responsibility requirement. Let me continue.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check an important question:

**Is anyone else claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or has anyone else applied for Child Benefit for him?**

This could include:
- The other parent (if you're separated or divorced)
- A grandparent or other relative
- Anyone else with responsibility for Alex

Are you the only person claiming for Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. It's just me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! You're the only person claiming for Alex. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check where Alex is living:

**Where is Alex currently living?**

Specifically, I need to know if:
- He's in hospital, OR
- He's in care (such as local authority care), OR
- He's fostered, OR
- He's living at home normally with you

Based on what you've told me so far, I expect he's living at home with you in Manchester, but I want to confirm.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's right - Alex lives at home with me here in Manchester. He's not in hospital, care, or anything like that.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is living at home with you normally. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council NOT paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, are you funding Alex's care yourself, or is the council providing financial support towards his accommodation or upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything - I'm looking after Alex myself and paying for everything.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! That's the final check complete. You meet all the eligibility requirements for Child Benefit for Alex. Let me confirm this outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Now let me provide you with your eligibility outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 **You're ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit!**

Great news! Based on the assessment, you **are eligible** to receive Child Benefit for **Alex**.

### Summary of Your Eligibility:

✅ **Alex's age**: 8 years old (under 16)
✅ **Employment**: Not working full-time (not employed at all)
✅ **Benefits**: Not receiving ESA or Universal Credit
✅ **Apprenticeship**: Not in any apprenticeship
✅ **Your residency**: You live in the UK (Manchester)
✅ **Responsibility**: You live with Alex and are responsible for him
✅ **No other claimants**: You're the only one claiming
✅ **Child's location**: Living at home normally with you
✅ **Council support**: The council is not paying towards his care

---

### **Next Steps - How to Claim:**

You can apply for Child Benefit online or by post:

1. **Apply online** at: www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim
2. **Or by post** using form CH2 (available from the same page)

### **Documents You'll Need:**

- Proof of your identity (passport, driving licence, etc.)
- Proof of Alex's identity (birth certificate or adoption certificate)

### **Important to Know:**

- **Payment frequency**: Child Benefit is usually paid every 4 weeks into your bank account
- **High Income Child Benefit Charge**: If you or a partner earns over £60,000 per year, you may be liable for a charge that reduces your Child Benefit. Be aware of this potential tax charge.

For more information, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
